recipes.name: Commit-reversal task on a maintained revision
recipes.summary: Undo a merged pull request on today's code to get a coding task inside an environment that already builds. Keep the candidate only if its target tests pass, fail and pass again across healthy, task and restored states.
recipes.background: Derive a coding task from a real merged pull request without rebuilding the environment at the old revision: undo the change on today's code, by patch reversal, code mapping or agent rewriting, so the task lives inside an environment that already builds and runs. A candidate is kept only if its target tests pass, fail and pass again across the healthy, task and restored states, which makes that triple the acceptance condition. Environment construction is graded by executable evidence on a maturity hierarchy rather than by a success flag, the discovered requirements are tracked in a typed dependency graph, and the construction procedure is replayed in a fresh environment to prove it reproduces.
recipes.produces: A coding task on the current revision whose target tests fail until the reverted feature is written again, with a replayable environment build.
when_to_use: the source is a maintained repository with a history of merged changes
rebuilding an environment at an old revision per task is too costly
you want tasks whose evaluation signal survives the move to a newer revision
not_when_to_use: the source has no test suite and no observable behaviour to reverse
the change spans so many files that reversing it on current code is meaningless
inputs: a repository checkout with history and a working test command
the merged pull request or its diff, together with its target tests
a replayable construction procedure for the environment

steps.title: Select a merged change with a test signal
steps.detail: Pick a pull request that added or modified tests, so the task carries an observable pass or fail condition instead of a subjective one.
steps.accept: The chosen pull request added or modified tests, and the command that runs those tests is known.

steps.title: Build the environment for the current revision
steps.detail: Install and validate the environment on today's code using an executable-evidence hierarchy: dependencies resolved, the project's tests partially executed, the main entry point actually running.
steps.accept: The project's main entry point runs and its test command executes successfully on the current revision.

steps.title: Track requirements in a typed dependency graph
steps.detail: Record each discovered requirement with its dependencies and state, discovered, satisfied or unresolved, so the construction state is not spread across the interaction history.
steps.accept: Every discovered requirement is recorded with its dependencies and its state: discovered, satisfied or unresolved.

steps.title: Reconstruct the pre-change state on the current revision
steps.detail: Reverse the patch, map the old code onto the new one, or have an agent rewrite the feature out, and keep the reconstruction only where the repository still builds and the targeted behaviour is gone.
steps.accept: The repository still builds at the reconstructed state and the targeted behaviour is gone.

steps.title: Apply the pass-fail-pass triple
steps.detail: Run the target tests in three states: healthy where they pass, task where they fail, and restored where they pass again. A candidate that fails in more than one of those states is not a task.
steps.accept: The target tests pass in the healthy state, fail in the task state and pass again in the restored state.

steps.title: Repair the environment, not the test
steps.detail: When the failure comes from a missing dependency or a broken build, extend the construction procedure and re-run, rather than editing the test to match the broken state.
steps.accept: The target test file is unmodified and the construction procedure has been extended so the build no longer breaks.

steps.title: Persist and replay the construction
steps.detail: Store the successful construction steps as a replayable procedure and apply it in a fresh environment; the reconstructed task must reproduce there with the same test behaviour.
steps.accept: The stored procedure rebuilds the environment in a fresh sandbox and the tests behave identically there.

curation_notes: Compare how the same agents score on the original revision and on the reconstructed task, and drop the pairs whose per-task agreement is poor.
Keep the target tests of the retained tasks disjoint, so one patch cannot pass two tasks in the set.
verifier: target tests pass on the healthy state, fail on the task state and pass again after restoration
the main entry point of the project executes successfully in the prepared environment
the stored construction procedure rebuilds the environment in a fresh sandbox and the tests behave identically
the repository builds in the task state, so the failure is behavioural rather than a broken build
pitfalls: rebuilding at the old revision makes every task expensive and brittle
reversing a change the current code has since restructured yields a task whose target tests fail for the wrong reason
a green build with no failing target test is a broken repo, not a task

source_papers.title: Change2Task: From Repository Changes to Executable Coding Agent Tasks and Environments
source_papers.note: undoing a merged pull request on today's code recreates the task inside a maintained revision; a task is kept only if its tests pass, fail and pass again across healthy, task and restored states

source_papers.title: HerAgent: Rethinking the Automated Environment Deployment via Hierarchical Test Pyramid
source_papers.note: Environment Maturity Hierarchy grades setup by executable evidence up to running the main entry point, instead of a weak dependency-installed signal

source_papers.title: Graph-Guided Repository Environment Construction
source_papers.note: typed dependency graph of execution requirements with persisted, replayable construction procedure, verified by applying the artifacts in a fresh environment

recipes.name: Depth-gated recursive terminal task composition
recipes.summary: Grow long-horizon terminal tasks by extending a verified seed: append the next workflow segment to its reference solution, realign verifier and instruction, validate in a fresh sandbox, and gate on depth not turns.
recipes.background: Grow long-horizon terminal tasks by extending a verified seed task: take its reference solution, append the next workflow segment, realign the verifier and the instruction to the new workflow, and validate the result in a fresh sandbox before accepting it as the next seed. Depth, not length, is the gating quantity, defined as the smallest turn cap under which the task still passes; turn counts alone mostly measure the habits of the model being graded. Writing the task one segment at a time inside the real environment keeps the instruction, the initial state, the reference solution and the verifier mutually consistent, which is what stops a synthesized task from being unsolvable or mis-graded.
recipes.produces: A long-horizon terminal task whose reference solution, instruction and verifier agree, with its depth recorded as the smallest passing turn cap.
when_to_use: long-horizon tasks are needed but verified seed tasks are scarce
the agent under evaluation is a terminal agent whose multi-turn behaviour is the target
a fresh-sandbox validation run per candidate task is affordable
not_when_to_use: the source is a single-command task with no sequential dependency between steps
no terminal harness is available to measure turn caps
inputs: a set of verified seed tasks with reference solutions and verifiers
a terminal environment that can run a candidate task from a fresh state
a way to run a task under a turn cap and record the outcome

steps.title: Start from verified seeds only
steps.detail: Every accepted task needs a working reference solution and a verifier that fails on the pristine environment; otherwise recursion compounds the errors of its inputs.
steps.accept: The seed task has a reference solution that passes and a verifier that fails on the pristine environment.

steps.title: Extend the reference solution
steps.detail: Add the next workflow segment to the reference solution so the new task endpoint is reachable by an executable path, not only describable in prose.
steps.accept: The extended reference solution runs end to end and reaches the new endpoint.

steps.title: Realign the verifier and the instruction
steps.detail: Rewrite both to match the extended workflow; a verifier still pointing at the old endpoint silently passes a workflow that was never completed.
steps.accept: The verifier checks the new endpoint and the instruction names the same workflow the reference solution performs.

steps.title: Write the task segment by segment in the real environment
steps.detail: Materialize each segment in the actual terminal and repair the environment when a segment cannot be executed, rather than describing the segment only in text.
steps.accept: Every segment of the workflow has been executed in the terminal and its commands are recorded.

steps.title: Validate in a fresh sandbox
steps.detail: Run the candidate from a clean environment and require the verifier to fail before the solution and to pass after it, so acceptance is based on execution rather than on inspection.
steps.accept: The verifier fails on the pristine environment and passes after the reference solution runs in a clean sandbox.

steps.title: Measure depth, not turns
steps.detail: Find the smallest turn cap under which the task still passes; that number is the depth. A task that passes within three turns has almost no depth, however many commands it takes.
steps.accept: The smallest turn cap under which the task still passes is recorded as the task's depth.

steps.title: Keep the artifact set consistent
steps.detail: Use the realized container state as the shared grounding for the instruction, the reference solution and the verifier, and regenerate only the artifact that is actually broken.
steps.accept: Instruction, reference solution and verifier are all regenerated from the realised container state and agree on the same endpoint.

curation_notes: Promote validated tasks into the seed pool and repeat, tracking the median reference-solution length and the median executed-command count per round as the growth signal.
Keep the workflows of one round distinct from each other and from the seeds they came from, so the set does not collapse into near-duplicates.
verifier: the verifier fails on the pristine environment and passes after the reference solution runs
the task's depth, measured as the smallest passing turn cap, is recorded and exceeds the chosen threshold
the command count executed by the reference solution matches the depth profile claimed for the task
the accepted task reproduces from its stored container state in a fresh sandbox
pitfalls: difficulty labelled by the model that generated the task does not measure the task
extending a task without touching the verifier leaves a check that passes on an unfinished workflow
recursive synthesis without re-validating in a fresh environment drifts between runs

source_papers.title: Recursive Synthesis for Long-Horizon Terminal Tasks
source_papers.note: extends the reference solution of a verified seed, realigns verifier and instruction, validates in a fresh sandbox and reuses accepted tasks as seeds for later rounds

source_papers.title: Is Your Long-Horizon Benchmark Really Deep? Measuring and Synthesizing Depth in Terminal Tasks
source_papers.note: depth defined as the smallest turn cap under which the task passes, turn counts reflecting model habits, and a generation agent writing each task one segment at a time in a real environment

source_papers.title: FACET: Preserving Source Intent and Executable State in Terminal Task Synthesis
source_papers.note: container state as shared grounding for instruction, reference solution and verifier, with execution-based validation and targeted repair instead of regenerating valid artifacts

recipes.name: Evidence-grounded Dockerized terminal blueprint
recipes.summary: Sample a blueprint across a capability taxonomy, ground it in evidence from real material, instantiate it as a Dockerized environment, then gate the tests on a rubric, a hint-conditional variant and a fail-to-pass check.
recipes.background: Sample a task blueprint across a capability taxonomy, ground it in evidence from real technical material, instantiate it as a Dockerized environment, then gate the tests: rubric-gated construction, hint-conditional filtering and a strict fail-to-pass check before the task is allowed into the set.
recipes.produces: A Dockerized task environment with rubric-gated tests that fail on the pristine environment and pass on the reference solution.
when_to_use: the source is code, a CLI tool, a repository or technical documentation
the task must run offline in a reproducible sandbox
you need many tasks and want them to be hard rather than retrofitted
not_when_to_use: the task needs live network access or real credentials
the source has no executable behaviour to anchor a task to
inputs: a capability taxonomy to sample from: domain, skill type, capability, engineering pillar
real technical material to ground each candidate in
a container runtime for the environments

steps.title: Sample blueprints from a taxonomy
steps.detail: Combine taxonomy dimensions rather than free-form prompting; surface-level retrofitting of artifacts is what produces vague instructions and shallow execution paths.
steps.accept: The blueprint's domain, skill type, capability and engineering pillar are recorded, and none of them is left blank.

steps.title: Ground the candidate in evidence
steps.detail: Do evidence-guided research over real material until the task has a concrete anchor: a real command, a real defect, a real data file. Reverse-engineering real recordings is one way to get anchors at scale.
steps.accept: The task names a concrete anchor taken from the real material: a real command, a real defect or a real data file.

steps.title: Write the blueprint
steps.detail: Specify the goal, the initial state, the expected artifacts and the difficulty, together with a reference solution written by a human-equivalent author, not by the same pass that wrote the task.
steps.accept: The goal, initial state, expected artifacts, difficulty and a separately authored reference solution are all written down.

steps.title: Instantiate the environment
steps.detail: Build the Docker image, the workdir, the seeded files and the offline constraints; every task gets its own environment rather than a shared one.
steps.accept: The Docker image builds, the workdir holds the seeded files, and the environment runs with no network access.

steps.title: Gate the tests on a rubric
steps.detail: Construct the test suite against a rubric for what counts as success, so the check is exhaustive rather than a single happy-path assertion.
steps.accept: The test suite covers every clause of the rubric and fails on the pristine environment.

steps.title: Filter with a hint-conditional variant
steps.detail: Run a variant with a hint; a task that is solved the same way with and without the hint carries no signal, so drop it or raise its difficulty.
steps.accept: The hinted and unhinted runs differ in outcome, so the task is kept or its difficulty is raised.

steps.title: Enforce fail-to-pass
steps.detail: The tests must fail on the pristine environment and pass on the reference solution. Anything else is not a task.
steps.accept: The tests fail on the pristine environment and pass after the reference solution runs.

curation_notes: Grow the set from existing environments with adaptive control of difficulty and diversity, instead of restarting from scratch each round.
Re-check the difficulty of the retained tasks as the solver population improves, because a frozen verifier stops discriminating.
verifier: strict fail-to-pass on the pristine environment
comprehensive tests, not a single assertion
reference solution that makes the tests pass from the environment workdir
pitfalls: ambiguous instructions and brittle tests come from retrofitting rather than grounding
a verifier that never fails teaches the agent nothing
frozen verifiers stop discriminating as the agent improves

source_papers.title: CLI-Universe: Towards Verifiable Task Synthesis Engine for Terminal Agents
source_papers.note: taxonomy sampling, evidence-guided grounding, rubric-gated tests, hint-conditional filtering, strict fail-to-pass

source_papers.title: Terminal-Bench: Benchmarking Agents on Hard, Realistic Tasks in Command Line Interfaces
source_papers.note: unique environment per task plus human-written solution and comprehensive tests

source_papers.title: TerminalWorld: Benchmarking Agents on Real-World Terminal Tasks
source_papers.note: reverse-engineers real terminal recordings to obtain authentic, scalable task anchors

source_papers.title: SETA: Scaling Environments for Terminal Agents
source_papers.note: shared verification mechanism plus an evolution pipeline that expands existing environments adaptively
